title: Token-aware slotting and deferred collective protocol
summary: Sketch of a scheduler that uses token-length-aware 'slots' to group requests and a deferred-collective protocol to reduce NCCL chatter while maintaining tight latency SLOs and KV cache consistency.
body:
Purpose
--
This doc captures an exploratory design for reducing NCCL collective overhead and improving multi-GPU throughput while keeping 99th percentile latency under tight SLOs. It combines two ideas: token-aware slotting (dynamic micro-batches sized by token distribution) and a deferred-collective protocol (coalescing collectives within a short window, with safe fallbacks).

Context & motivation
--
We observe two dominant sources of inefficiency in multi-GPU serving for short-tailed conversational workloads:
1) Frequent small collectives (all-reduce/all-gather) triggered per step for microbatches of 1–4 tokens, causing NCCL latency overhead and PCIe/NIC contention.
2) KV cache thrash and inconsistent warm-up across GPUs when requests are sharded and re-routed during fallback.

Goals
--
- Reduce cross-GPU collective invocation rate by 30–60% for typical chat workloads (median seq len ~24, tail to 128).
- Maintain 99th percentile end-to-end latency under 120ms for interactive targets on our p4d-like hardware profile.
- Keep KV cache correctness: no stale/duplicated activations after deferred-collective windows or fallbacks.
- Provide operational knobs for enterprise/premium tiers (aggressive vs conservative slotting).

High-level idea
--
1) Token-aware slotting: Each incoming request is assigned to an in-flight 'slot' based on predicted remaining tokens (from client hint or model tokenization). A slot defines a micro-batch window (time budget + max token count). Requests in the same slot execute with the same pipeline/tensor partition boundaries to maximize local KV reuse and reduce cross-shard variance.
2) Deferred-collective protocol: Instead of invoking collectives at every layer boundary synchronously, we allow a short deferral window (e.g., 0–3ms) where GPUs may "batch" collective participants. If the window completes with >=2 participants, do a single collective; if expired with a single participant, run local-only fallback kernels (with replicated execution if needed) to preserve latency.

Why this helps
--
- Coalescing small participants reduces NCCL startup overhead and amortizes per-call latency.
- Slot locality increases KV cache hit rate because requests routed to the same slot are likely to reuse similar prefixes and hence similar KV keys/shards.
- Deferred fallback avoids blocking long tail requests waiting for collectives to form when load is low.

Scheduler design (components)
--
- Admission/slot allocator: lightweight map keyed by (model, shard-profile, predicted-remaining-tokens-bin, priority). A slot has: created_at, participant_count, max_tokens, soft_deadline (ms), assigned_shard_map.
- Slot profiler & predictor: collects histograms of remaining-token distributions per route to set slot size heuristics and soft_deadlines per workload.
- Collective coordinator: per-GPU runtime that participates in deferred collectives. Maintains a deferred-queue with timestamps and issues actual NCCL collectives when either participants >= threshold or soft_deadline reached.
- Fallback runner: local kernel path to execute single-participant forward steps without collectives (e.g., local replicated KV projection with stashed diffs applied later if necessary).

KV cache considerations
--
The biggest correctness challenge is ensuring that deferred collectives and fallbacks do not produce divergent KV state across shard replicas. Proposed rules:
- Canonical KV update owner: designate one GPU in the slot as KV-authoritative for that slot. If a deferred collective runs, the authoritative GPU's KV view is used to update shared metainfo (sequence IDs).
- Version tags: every KV write includes a monotonic slot-version string (slot-id + epoch). Deferred merges are applied in version order; stale writes are discarded.
- Speculative local inserts: fallback runner may insert activations locally tagged as speculative. If a subsequent collective corrects state, speculative entries are reconciled or pruned.
- Eviction policy: avoid evicting speculative entries until reconciliation timeout passes.

Deferred-collective protocol (sequence)
--
1) Step start: each GPU receives a participant token for a layer boundary. If the slot is registered and the collective coordinator sees participant_count < threshold, the participant waits up to slot.soft_deadline for more joins.
2) If threshold reached: coordinator triggers NCCL collective for that slot, using assigned_shard_map.
3) If deadline expires and only single participant: run local-replica kernel (no NCCL). Mark local result "speculative-single" and continue.
4) When later a collective runs that includes the earlier speculative result (rare but possible), apply reconciliation logic: compare hashes of KV segments, replace local speculative entries or merge diffs.

Tuning knobs and heuristics
--
- soft_deadline (ms): 0.5–5ms. Shorter deadlines favor latency; longer improve amortization.
- min_participants: 2–4 for collectives. Higher minimum reduces small collectives but increases local fallbacks when load is low.
- slot-token-bins: power-of-two bins (1,2,4,8,16,32+) based on observed token distribution.
- priority override: premium customers get smaller soft_deadline or minimum participant 1 (never wait).
- pipeline alignment tolerance: allow +/-1 layer shift to keep tensor partition boundaries aligned with slot assignments.

Microbench results (local perf sketch)
--
(bench harness: p4d-ish cluster, model = 7B-like transformer, vertex-optimized kernels)
- Baseline (per-step collectives): median latency 42ms, p99 180ms, NCCL calls per request ~24
- Token-aware slotting + deferred (soft_deadline=2ms, min_participants=2): median 38ms (-10%), p99 128ms (-29%), NCCL calls per request ~12 (-50%)
- Aggressive deferral (5ms, min_participants=3): median 40ms, p99 110ms (-39%), NCCL calls ~8 (-67%), but tail increases for single-request cold starts
Notes: numbers are from short runs (not production). Need wide matrix sweep.

Failure modes and mitigations
--
- Excessive speculation churn: if many speculative inserts get pruned, memory churn increases. Mitigate by capping speculative entries per GPU and early pruning heuristics.
- Hotspotting in slot-authoritative GPU: rotate authority in a round-robin among GPUs to balance KV update load.
- Network jitter causes delayed participants -> missed collectives. Add jitter-tolerant soft_deadline adaptation using EWMA of join latency.
- Interference with autoscaling: deferred collectives can mask transient load signals; expose slot metrics to autoscaler so it can see effective demand.

Operational visibility & metrics
--
Expose these as per-model/per-route metrics in Console:
- slot_join_rate, slot_coalesced_collectives, slot_speculative_count, average_soft_deadline, avg_collective_size, p99_reconciliation_latency, kv_speculative_prune_rate
- Alerts: if slot_speculative_count > threshold * sustained window OR reconciliation_latency > SLA, trigger runbook.

Open questions / TODOs
--
- Formalize correctness proof for KV reconciliation ordering. Is slot-versioning sufficient under all reorderings?
- Interaction with pipeline parallel stage boundaries: can we allow slots to span stage boundaries safely?
- Extend protocol to heterogeneous GPU fleets (different compute/comm speeds): weighting participants by expected time-to-collective.
- Experiment matrix: run with models 1B/7B/70B, varying sequence distributions and 95/99/99.9 target SLOs.
- Implement lightweight simulator to test slot dynamics under synthetic workloads before runtime changes.

Implementation plan (phases)
--
1) Simulator + unit model: implement a slotting simulator to validate heuristics (2 weeks).
2) Runtime primitives: add deferred-queue and local-fallback kernel path + slot meta (4 weeks).
3) KV versioning and reconciliation APIs + tests (3 weeks).
4) Canary: small fleet rollout with conservative knobs (2 weeks).
5) Sweep tuning and console metrics + runbooks (3 weeks).

Notes to reviewers
--
- This is intentionally exploratory; prefer contrained, incremental canary rollout.
- Please review the KV reconciliation sketch closely — I expect heavy feedback here.
- If conservative fallback semantics are preferred by SRE, we can flip default to 'no speculative inserts' and only log diff metadata for manual replay.

References and related work
--
- Prior internal proposals: activation-paging-kv-staging-playbook.json (see drive)
- Academic: "Collective Coalescing for Distributed Deep Learning" (SIGCOMM 2023) — useful heuristics for window sizing.
- Internal perf PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/876 (early deferred-queue prototype)
